spec.title: PROP-074 — General local derivatives: required family matrix

status.comment: M-10-A.1 matrix accepted through Zap WorkAccepted revision 276 on 2026-10-14; general derivative implementation remains open.

section.title: Ownership and scope
section.p: VibeVM owns source identity, packages, composition, workspace and context. Zap owns goals, plans, logical task concurrency and acceptance. PodBay owns physical processes, lifecycle, resources and I/O. This document defines VibeVM resource requirements; it introduces neither a planning authority nor process controls. Basis: [PROJECT-BOUNDARIES#SOURCE-VERSUS-PLAN](PROJECT-BOUNDARIES.xml#SOURCE-VERSUS-PLAN) and [PROJECT-BOUNDARIES#VIBEVM-OWNER](PROJECT-BOUNDARIES.xml#VIBEVM-OWNER).

The five families below are source interpretations and resource shapes, not the aggregator/lang/mcp package roles of PROP-028. Its new-name/new-identity and family compatibility distinctions still apply: a local derivative cannot reuse an upstream coordinate for different bytes. Fixtures are design data, not installable packages, grants or production manifest syntax.

section.title: Four distinct bindings
section.p: Original capture/base identity: retain the exact captured bytes, selected interpretation, original package/version and source path or tree inventory. Never edit an installed upstream slot or rewrite an upstream content hash to describe local content. PROP-045#HASH-LAW already distinguishes source hashes from transformed output hashes.

Local authored ownership: a distinct local coordinate and author own the replacement bytes and their relation to the base. Authored content must survive deletion of disposable derived output. A composed-skill cache or transformed slot is not the sole home of local edits. Fixture inventory hashes are explicitly fixture-only; they do not claim to be production package content hashes or verified capture proofs.

Compatibility target: bind the exact base identity and selected path, named export or tree being replaced. Compatibility is an explicit claim about use, not identity equality, upstream endorsement or authorization. A changed base requires an incompatibility/rebase decision; do not silently move a byte span onto a different capture. Vibe fact addresses in the local coordinate remain separate from upstream facts.

Downstream activation: passive creation, show and diff produce inspectable data. Context selection, installation, skill projection, deployment or execution remain separate existing consumer operations. Derivation neither hydrates dependencies nor executes code nor inherits upstream grants. These requirements do not pretend that a general derive/show/diff/rebase/apply API already exists.

section.title: Eligibility without a new permission language
section.p: A sealed source permits a separately owned local derivative; sealing protects the original capture and identity. Neither absent demand evidence nor a sealed flag is a new permission gate. Every fixture starts with sealed=true and demand_evidence=null. Later executable cases must also toggle sealing and show equal derivative eligibility while leaving the original untouched.

Existing source validity, exact selection, compatibility, path containment, collision and downstream ownership checks still apply. Their failures must name the actual invalid input or incompatible consumer contract. Do not translate them into invented priority levels, demand approval or a global derivative permission system.

section.title: Existing seams and their limits
section.p: vibe-specdoc owns ordinary CommonMark parsing and resolve_export: a named nested heading selection carries a span and SHA-256 of the parsed capture. Its xml_data module provides inspect_xml_data and preserve_opaque; optional inspection never replaces raw bytes. Neither mechanism performs general authored replacement.

vibe-workspace::vibedeps::derived selects descriptors before conversion. Its selection module classifies Commonmark, XmlData and Opaque as Raw; declared Vibe sources alone enter the pivot. replay_declared_captured is a pure conversion seam, explicitly not a capture proof. The transform module calls vibe-specdoc frontends/backends; the overlay module changes fact adoption status, not arbitrary fact bodies. Current slot records retain source/output accounting. A transformed slot is not a local authored derivative service.

vibe-spec::resolver::lookup owns canonical document paths and refuses same-document representation collisions and ambiguous lookup. It is not a priority engine for local replacements. vibe-agent-projection::pkgskill owns receipt-based update/uninstall and preserves unowned neighbors. projection::hydrate_declared_skill composes a local adapter with embedded resources into a content-keyed tree and refuses duplicate targets. It may hydrate through its provider, so it is not the passive derivative operation to invoke here. Resource composition does not establish general replacement precedence.

section.title: Required families and later executable cases
CommonMark
section.p: Scenario commonmark: replace Usage prose in guide.md while preserving Reference and fenced shell bytes. Existing seam: vibe-specdoc::commonmark::CommonMarkDoc::resolve_export for usage.v1 at Guide/Usage. Missing owner behavior: vibe-workspace must bind separately authored replacement content to the original capture/export witness and consumer selection; vibe-specdoc remains the structural selector owner.

Later executable case: resolve both snapshots, assert changed full-source hash, exact selected bytes and unchanged sibling/fence content; reject missing or ambiguous heading selection and stale capture binding. Ordinary Vibe-shaped prose and code remain data, never facts or commands.

section.title: XML data
section.p: Scenario xml-data: replace timeout 30 with 90 while retaining UTF-8 BOM, comments, entity spelling, whitespace and script text. Existing seams: inspect_xml_data and descriptor Raw copying. Missing owner behavior: vibe-workspace must retain provenance and local ownership for whole-byte replacement. Optional structure in vibe-specdoc is not an XML rewriting engine.

Later executable case: inspect base/local/expected through the XML-data seam and compare exact raw bytes. Unavailable optional inspection must retain captured data and diagnostics; it must not silently convert ordinary XML into the Vibe dialect. No entity fetching or execution follows from data inspection.

section.title: Vibe-spec
section.p: Scenario vibe-spec: replace RETRY body in local POLICY.xml, retaining its code fence and keeping upstream POLICY#RETRY unchanged. Existing seams: vibe-specdoc pivot parsing/emission, vibe-workspace declared conversion and adoption-status overlays, and vibe-spec canonical lookup. Missing owner behavior: vibe-workspace must bind authored body replacement and compatibility to a distinct local identity; vibe-spec must resolve the selected local document without impersonating the upstream address. A status overlay cannot implement this body edit.

Later executable case: parse the local Vibe document, assert the new body and retained anchor/fence, and verify the base body/address still resolves in its own coordinate. Exercise equivalent Markdown/XML representation through the existing pivot; refuse simultaneous representations of one selected document. This is semantic conversion, not a promise of lossless XML spelling.

section.title: Opaque file
section.p: Scenario opaque-file: replace payload.bin containing invalid UTF-8, NUL, CRLF and code-like bytes. Existing seams: preserve_opaque and vibe-workspace descriptor Raw copying. Missing owner behavior: vibe-workspace needs the same separately owned replacement lifecycle for arbitrary byte arrays, without text decoding or Vibe parsing.

Later executable case: compare every byte and independent base/local hashes; passive show/diff reports a binary change without interpreting or running code. A text-only implementation cannot satisfy this row.

section.title: Nested tree
section.p: Scenario nested-tree: replace a nested binary palette and adapter body, remove docs/obsolete.txt, add docs/local.txt, preserve docs/keep.txt and scripts/helper.sh. An unowned FOREIGN.txt at a downstream target must survive update and uninstall. Existing seams: pkgskill snapshots, selected resource composition and receipt-based reconciliation. Missing owner behavior: vibe-workspace needs a general authored tree derivative with explicit replacement/deletion and base binding; vibe-agent-projection must consume the selected result using its existing receipts.

Later executable case: assert exact relative-path inventory and bytes, explicit removal of only owned paths, retained unowned neighbor, collision refusal and safe path handling. Delete disposable output, regenerate from retained authored input and obtain the same result. Resource collision refusal must not be replaced by implicit last-writer-wins. The script remains inert bytes.

section.title: Fixture and implementation evidence
section.p: fixtures/next/derivatives/manifest.json binds five base/local/expected inventories, compatibility targets, missing owner behavior and later executable requirements. validate.py checks design data and exact bytes; pure_seams.rs exercises existing parsers on these fixture bytes. Neither is a general derivative implementation or five new compiled derivative tests. No fixture is installed or activated.

The three selected existing Rust tests establish only ownership reconciliation, CommonMark export capture binding and XML raw-byte preservation. Future implementation must create each derivative through its owning service, exercise sealed and unsealed bases with absent demand, verify unchanged upstream captures, reject stale compatibility, preserve local source after cache deletion, and prove passive inspection has no hydration/execution/activation effects. Test names and evidence must distinguish those future requirements from today's existing mechanism checks.

This document adds design anchors without fact declarations, adoption records, dependency declarations, boot registration or implementation closure claims. Focused XML/fixture validation is the appropriate oracle for this change. Whole-project composition and exhaustive fact checks remain conditional on actual changes to those mechanisms.
